Under the EUDR country benchmarking implementing act of 22 May 2025, Brazil is 'standard risk'; only Belarus, Myanmar, North Korea and Russia are high risk (140 low, about 50 standard). The EP objected to the methodology in July 2025.
The EUDR covers cattle, cocoa, coffee, oil palm, rubber, soya and wood and derived products.
Brazil exported a record 23.3 Mt of soybean meal in 2025, of which 11.7 Mt (50.2%) went to the EU; EU buyers front-loaded purchases ahead of the EUDR.

PRODES 2025 (Aug 2024-Jul 2025) put Legal Amazon clear-cut deforestation at 5,796 km², down 11.08% from 6,518 km², the fourth straight decline and the lowest in 11 years; Cerrado was 7,235 km² (-11.49%).

DETER alerts for Aug 2025-Jul 2026 covered 2,874 km² in the Amazon, down 36.87% and the lowest since the series began in 2015 (Mato Grosso -49%, Para -25%, Roraima +32%); Cerrado alerts fell 7.8% to about 5,119 km². The PRODES 2026 rate was not yet published.
Lula signed the General Environmental Licensing Law (Lei 15.190/2025) in Aug 2025 with 63 vetoes; on 27 Nov 2025 Congress overturned 52 of them (Chamber 295-167, Senate 52-15).
CADE imposed a preventive measure on 18 Aug 2025 suspending the Amazon Soy Moratorium as a possible cartel; a federal court injunction overturned the suspension on 25 Aug 2025.

Mato Grosso Law 12.709/2024, which strips tax incentives from Soy Moratorium signatories, took effect on 1 Jan 2026; in January 2026 Abiove and its trader members (ADM, Bunge, Cargill, COFCO, LDC) moved to exit the moratorium.

In Aug 2026 the STF (ADIs 7774/7775, rapporteur Dino's view prevailing) held the Soy Moratorium compatible with the Constitution while upholding the Mato Grosso and Rondonia laws restricting incentives to its participants.

The Tropical Forest Forever Facility was launched at the Belem leaders' summit (Nov 2025) with about US$5.5bn pledged on day one: Norway US$3bn over 10 years (conditional), Brazil and Indonesia US$1bn each, France EUR500m. This is well short of the US$25bn sponsor target.

Flavio Bolsonaro's programme does not mention climate change, the NDC or the Paris Agreement. The Climate Observatory flags 7 anti-environment proposals, and he pledged to end 'amarras ambientais' while targeting zero illegal deforestation by 2029.

The CBAM Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2025/2083, in force 20 Oct 2025) added a 50 t/year per-importer mass threshold; the definitive period started on 1 Jan 2026, with certificate sales from Feb 2027 covering 2026 imports. Covered goods are iron/steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen.
A CNI analysis estimated CBAM would affect more than US$3bn of Brazilian exports to the EU (2023 data), almost all iron and steel; CNI calls the mechanism discriminatory.
EU imports of iron and steel from Brazil were US$1.74bn in 2025, including US$341m of semi-finished products and US$224m of pig iron.

Brazil's pig iron exports hit a record 4.05 Mt in 2025 (+8%), and lower-carbon Brazilian pig iron is gaining EU share (especially Italy) as Russian pig iron is banned from 2026, so the CBAM cost per tonne is lower than for rival suppliers.
The EU ETS allowance price was about EUR83.6/t on 5 Oct 2026, in a range of about EUR74 (May avg) to EUR85 during mid-2026.

Brazil's Lei 15.042/2024 created the SBCE cap-and-trade system: regulation in 2025-26, operationalisation in 2027, emissions reporting in 2028-29 and the first National Allocation Plan from 2030; the Finance Ministry proposed sector scope in May 2026.

Brazil's exports to Argentina were US$18.1bn in 2025 (+31.4%), making Argentina the third-largest destination with autos the lead item; Brazil swung from a US$142m deficit in 2024 to a US$2.44bn surplus in 2025.

No formal dispute has been filed.
Mercosur foreign ministers agreed in Buenos Aires (Apr 2025) to temporarily let each member add up to 50 more tariff lines to its national CET exception list, citing the global trade war.

claim: The Mercosur-EFTA FTA was signed in Rio de Janeiro on 16 Sep 2025 (talks concluded 2 Jul 2025), improving market access for over 97% of exports; its entry into force is pending.
Mercosur-UAE CEPA talks (launched Jul 2024) were about 80% complete after the 4th round in Nov 2025 and had not been concluded as of Jul 2026; non-oil trade was US$6.2bn in 2025.
In Argentina's 26 Oct 2025 midterms, Milei's La Libertad Avanza won about 40.7-40.8% nationally and 64 Chamber seats (95 total bloc), a strengthened position.

Milei attended Flavio Bolsonaro's campaign launch (Jul 2026), and Brazil downgraded diplomatic ties with Argentina in Aug 2026 after Milei called Lula a thief. Milei congratulated Flavio on the first round on 5 Oct 2026, and his circle sees a Flavio win speeding Mercosur revision and outside deals.

claim: Uruguay's Orsi backs Milei's push to make Mercosur more flexible so members can sign their own deals (Asia/CPTPP), while Paraguay's Pena demands flexibility from partners for an 'equitable' share of EU quotas.
Crude oil was Brazil's top export in 2025 at US$44.67bn (-0.7%), ahead of soybeans at US$43.54bn and iron ore at US$28.9bn; total exports were a record US$348.7bn with a US$68.3bn surplus.
Brazil exported about 726m barrels of crude in 2025 (1.98 mb/d, +10% y/y), with China taking about 45% (about 880 kb/d).

Ibama granted Petrobras an operating licence in Oct 2025 to drill the Morpho well in block FZA-M-59 (Foz do Amazonas, about 175 km off Amapa); Petrobras reported oil discoveries there in Aug 2026 and again in Oct 2026, and has applied for three more wells while federal prosecutors (MPF) seek suspension of the licence.
Petrobras' 2026-30 business plan sets capex of US$109bn (US$78bn E&P), with oil output peaking at 2.7 mb/d in 2028 and total output at 3.4 MMboe/d in 2028-29.
Brazil's CNPE approved joining the OPEC+ Charter of Cooperation in Feb 2025; this is a dialogue platform with no production-cut obligations.

Flavio's campaign coordinator Rogerio Marinho said on 18 Aug 2026 there is 'no plan to privatise Petrobras'. The 75-page programme does not mention Petrobras but proposes restarting the national privatisation programme for more than 20 SOEs (excluding Petrobras and Caixa) and reviewing Petrobras' structure.

Under Jair Bolsonaro (2019-22) Petrobras was not privatised, but it lost control of BR Distribuidora (Jul 2019, fully sold 2021), sold the RLAM refinery to Mubadala for US$1.65bn (2021) and sold the TAG and NTS pipeline networks.
Brent averaged US$117.29/bbl in Apr 2026 and briefly touched US$126.41 on 30 Apr 2026, driven by the US-Israel war with Iran, the Strait of Hormuz closure and the US blockade of Iranian ports.

On 5 Oct 2026, after Flavio led the first round, USD/BRL fell about 4-4.5% to about R$5.00 (from about 5.22), the Ibovespa rose about 7.8% to a record 207,074 (intraday about 209,600) and DI futures fell more than 100bp.

JPMorgan scenarios: fiscal adjustment (seen as a Flavio case) would mean BRL +6%, yields about 13% and equities +50%, while fiscal deterioration would mean BRL -6%, yields about 15.5% and equities -21%. BTG sees B3 up to +45% on a Flavio win.
On 16 Sep 2026 Copom cut the Selic by 25bp to 13.75%, citing Middle East conflict uncertainty.
Official first-round shares on 4 Oct 2026 were reported as Flavio Bolsonaro 47.03% and Lula 45.16% of valid votes, with the run-off on 25 Oct 2026.
